comment: Tile sources as data (roadmap 1.2). `id` is part of every tile key and of the disk cache: never reuse or renumber one. `kind`: imagery (photographs, faded smoothly between levels), map (drawn maps with text), elevation (Terrarium heights), overlay (drawn over the basemap). `access.template` takes {z}, {x} and {y}. Strings ending in `_key` name a translated text. `max_parallel` caps downloads from the source at once (the OpenStreetMap tile policy asks for at most two).

sources.name: Satellite (Esri World Imagery)
sources.notes: blankTile=false: missing tiles answer 404 instead of the 'Map data not yet available' image, so coarser imagery stands in. Distinct tiles exist past z17 (probed z18-z20).

sources.name: Streets (OpenStreetMap)
sources.notes: The OpenStreetMap tile usage policy forbids bulk prefetching.

sources.name: Earth at Night (NASA Black Marble)
sources.attribution: Night lights: NASA Earth Observatory / GIBS (VIIRS Black Marble)
sources.notes: NASA GIBS, layer VIIRS_Black_Marble (Worldview: 'Earth at Night', 500 m, a 2012 and a 2016 composite; 2020-2022 answer 404, checked 2026-11-04), Web Mercator tile matrix GoogleMapsCompatible_Level8. The app's time picks the edition.

sources.name: Arctic imagery (NASA Blue Marble with shaded relief and bathymetry, polar)
sources.notes: EPSG:3413 polar stereographic, not Web Mercator: the renderer computes these keys itself (globecraft-render polar.rs) for the cap past the Mercator limit. Level 0 is 2x2 tiles of 512 px over +-4194304 m (8192 m per pixel), level 4 is 512 m per pixel; level 5 answers 400 (checked 2026-11-04). The bathymetry layer, not BlueMarble_NextGeneration: its shaded blue ocean matches Esri's at the cap's edge, where the plain layer's near-black Arctic Ocean showed as a dark disc.

sources.name: Antarctic imagery (NASA Blue Marble with shaded relief and bathymetry, polar)
sources.notes: EPSG:3031 polar stereographic; same grid as polar_north.
